title: Xi's Mystery Black-Covered Limousine Lands in Delhi Ahead of BRICS Summit
excerpt: The Hongqi N701, China's secretive presidential limousine, arrived under covers for Xi Jinping's first India visit in seven years, with Modi set to host him on Saturday evening.
body:
• Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on September 12 for the 18th BRICS Summit — his first visit to India in seven years — and images of his motorcade cars arriving under black covers went viral on social media.
  • The car at the center of the attention is the Hongqi N701, a bespoke presidential limousine built by China's FAW under its Hongqi ("Red Flag") marque, estimated at over 18 feet long and three tonnes, with bullet-resistant glass and reinforced bodywork.
  • Almost all technical details of the N701 remain secret: Hongqi has never confirmed its engine, power output, or precise level of ballistic protection, and the car is produced in very limited numbers for state use only.
  • Xi's car is one of two ultra-secure state limousines in Delhi this week — Vladimir Putin's bulletproof Aurus Senat is also on the summit's roads — with Modi set to hold bilateral talks with Xi on Saturday evening.

Images of Chinese President Xi Jinping's convoy arriving in New Delhi under black covers have gone viral on social media, turning the Chinese leader's car into one of the first talking points of the 18th BRICS Summit. Xi began a two-day visit to New Delhi on September 12 to attend the summit, his first trip to India in seven years, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi scheduled to host him for bilateral talks on Saturday evening.

The vehicle drawing the cameras is the Hongqi N701, a heavily guarded, ultra-exclusive state limousine built under profound secrecy by FAW Group's Hongqi marque and reserved for China's top leadership. Reports describe the car as engineered to withstand gunfire, chemical attacks, and explosive threats — though, as with nearly everything about the N701, those claims are unconfirmed by the manufacturer.

A fortress that doubles as a statement

The security motorcades of world leaders double as displays of strength during foreign visits. For decades, the armored Cadillac One of the American president — "The Beast" — commanded the global spotlight. The Hongqi N701, estimated at more than 18 feet long and weighing over three tonnes, is China's answer: bullet-resistant glass, reinforced bodywork, and specially secured wheels and tires, with some reports also crediting it with independent life-support and secure communication systems.

What sets the N701 apart even among presidential limousines is how little is officially known. Some reports suggest a 6.0-litre V12 engine producing around 408 horsepower; others say the powertrain could be a V8. China has not officially revealed the engine, power output, or precise level of ballistic protection. The limousine is produced in very limited numbers and is not available to private buyers — a dedicated state vehicle in the truest sense.

Why the black covers?

The mystery covers, which triggered much of the online speculation, are standard practice rather than a sign of an extraordinary threat. Heavy covers shield vehicles from dust, sunlight, rain, and possible damage while being unloaded, moved through airport facilities, or transported on carriers — and for highly protected state cars, they also limit unnecessary exposure before official use. Similar footage of Xi's car being transported under security covers emerged during his visit to Malaysia.

"The N701 is estimated to be more than 18 feet long and weigh over three tonnes. It is believed to have heavy armour, bullet-resistant glass and reinforced bodywork, along with independent life-support and secure communication systems."

— India Today, on Xi Jinping's state limousine

Notably, when Xi arrived in New Delhi on September 12, his official car was seen uncovered during the welcome and convoy movements — the black covers are applied during transport, not during use.

Hongqi's India connection

The N701 is not the first Hongqi to touch Indian soil. Modi himself travelled in a Hongqi L5 — another flagship of the marque — during his visit to Tianjin for the SCO Summit in 2025, and Xi had used an L5 during his 2019 visit to India for the informal talks with the Prime Minister in Mahabalipuram. Hongqi, meaning "Red Flag," was established in 1958 by First Automotive Works specifically to build cars for China's political leadership; its early models served senior Communist Party officials and visiting foreign leaders before the brand was revived as a premium domestic marque.

Xi is not the only leader arriving in an armored flagship. Vladimir Putin's Aurus Senat — the Russian president's bulletproof, blast-resistant limousine — is also on Delhi's roads for the summit. Modi has history with both cars: he travelled with Putin in the Aurus during the SCO Summit in China in 2025.

What's next

The cars will fade from view as the summit's substance takes over. Xi's delegation includes Cai Qi, a member of the Communist Party's Politburo Standing Committee, and Foreign Minister Wang Yi. Saturday evening's bilateral with Modi will be watched for signals on the India-China relationship seven years after Xi's last visit — the limousine, secretive as ever, will be waiting outside.
image_caption: Chinese President Xi Jinping. His motorcade drew attention in Delhi as leaders gathered ahead of the BRICS summit.
nri_angle: The summit's outcomes on trade, currency settlement, and India-China ties will shape the economic environment that Indian businesses and professionals operate in.
